messages:
Maya: seeing a flood of 5xxs and timeouts for hosted inference since 11:02 PDT. Error rate + latency spike on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. App logs show memcached/mcache timeouts and kv ops blocking. Anyone oncall? :rotating_light:
Samir: yep alerts fired. memcached cluster RTT jumped and connections hitting ECONNREFUSED. Grafana shows kv_latency P99 -> 1.2s.
Olivia: which region/cluster? can you paste an example request_id and a small repro?
Maya: region: us-west-2, cluster: mc-west-2a. example request_id: req_0ab3f2c4. Repro curl (this returns 504/gateway timeout):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
Logs around the error: 
```
[2024-07-12T18:02:13Z] warn kv_client: memcached timeout after 1200ms for key=kv_prefix_v1:ctx_abc
[2024-07-12T18:02:13Z] error serve: downstream error: gateway timeout (504) req=req_0ab3f2c4
```
Samir: looking at memcached nodes, one node returned too many connections then flapped. Trying quick mitigation: flip cache bypass for prefix kv_prefix_v1 so runtime falls back to origin model path.
Olivia: good call. How do we flip that? admin API?
Samir: yeah admin API endpoint: 
```
# disable prefix caching for the faulty prefix
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/v1/cache/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prefix":"kv_prefix_v1","enabled":false}'
```
Maya: applied that at 11:10. infra-bot: posted deployment notice.
infra-bot: [ALERT] Cache config update: disabled prefix kv_prefix_v1 by Maya at 2024-07-12T18:10:05Z.
Samir: after disable, error rate dropped quickly but token/time costs increased because cache miss rate spiked. Traffic back to 200s for most endpoints. Still seeing a few 5xx from a different path where code didn't handle cache timeouts properly.
Carlos: we should also adjust client-side timeouts and add circuit breaker. Proposal: set KV client timeout to 100ms and circuit-break to short-circuit after 3 consecutive failures. I'll open a PR for runtime.
Olivia: can you paste memcached stats you saw?
Samir: ran quick check: 
```
echo "stats" | nc memcached-01.internal 11211
STAT pid 12345
STAT uptime 86400
STAT malloc_fails 0
STAT curr_connections 1400
STAT total_connections 30000
STAT connection_structures 1403
STAT cmd_get 120000
STAT get_hits 110000
STAT get_misses 10000
STAT evictions 4300
STAT bytes 987654321
END
```
Samir: evictions are high and curr_connections also high; suspect client storm + small memory causing evictions. We'll scale memcached and rotate the instance.
deploy-bot: started rolling restart of memcached-asg mc-west-2a at 2024-07-12T18:12:30Z by Samir.
Maya: customer impact: support team seeing multiple customers reporting 5xx on hosted endpoints. We should notify enterprise customers.
support-oncall: drafting message to affected customers. Early mitigation: disable prefix cache and restart memcached. Update sent to customers at 18:20 PT.
Samir: memcached nodes restarted and scaled by +2 nodes at 18:18. After restart, memcached P99 latency down to ~20ms. All green on main dashboards.
Maya: verified main endpoints back to 200s. Reproduced earlier Gateway timeouts are gone.
Carlos: created PR #4523 to add: default KV timeout 100ms, circuit-break threshold 3, fallback path to bypass cache immediately when errors exceed threshold. Will canary in eng runtime next deploy.
Olivia: couple of follow-ups: 1) postmortem owner? 2) add alert rule for memcached eviction rate > 1000 over 5m and kv_latency p99 > 300ms. 3) add automated fallback in router for cache dependency.
Samir: I'll own postmortem. Silva/SRE can do alert rule.
Maya: action items captured: Samir -> postmortem + retro, Carlos -> PR + canary, Olivia -> update runbook and alerts, support-oncall -> customer follow-up thread.
support-oncall: customers updated, legal/security looped for any data concerns (none expected).
Maya: thanks all, marking incident as mitigated at 18:25 PT. Will file full incident writeup in incidents channel tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
